Sam Altman’s Track Record: Promises Broken, Missions Betrayed.
•  Co-founded OpenAI as a nonprofit for humanity — open-source, safety-first, no profit motive. Turned it into a closed for-profit empire tied to Microsoft, gutted the safety team, and got fired by his own board for “not being consistently candid.”
•  Pushed Worldcoin — iris-scanning people in developing countries for crypto tokens. Accused of deceptive data harvesting and exploitation.
•  Earlier startups (Loopt) and Y Combinator role: board members and colleagues repeatedly called out deceptive behavior and conflicts of interest.
Pattern is clear. Now facing Elon in court over the original OpenAI mission. The mask is off.




Elon Musk (@elonmusk)

Scam Altman and Greg Stockman stole a charity. Full stop. 

Greg got tens of billions of stock for himself and Scam got dozens of OpenAI side deals with a piece of the action for himself, Y Combinator style. After this lawsuit, Scam will also be awarded tens of billions in stock directly. 

The fundamental question is simply this: 

Do you want to set legal precedent in the United States that it is ok to loot a charity? If so, you undermine all charitable giving in the United States forever.

Then they stole the charity.

BREAKING: Emirates is bringing Starlink to the A380.

The airline is upgrading its flagship aircraft with high-speed Starlink Wi-Fi, aiming for what it calls “better-than-home” internet at 40,000 feet. This is a serious shift from the slow, unstable connections most passengers expect.

Each A380 can carry up to 3 Starlink antennas, unlocking a massive jump in performance. Speeds could improve by up to 1000x compared to older systems, making streaming, gaming, video calls and real work possible in the air.

The rollout starts in 2026 as part of a broader fleet upgrade. This is one of the biggest steps yet toward turning in-flight Wi-Fi into something people actually rely on.
